Ghost-vendor fraud: create a fake vendor then pay it.

windows_server.title: Minimum password length ≥ 14
windows_server.remediation: GPO: Computer Config > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Account Policies > Password Policy > Minimum password length = 14

windows_server.title: Password history ≥ 24
windows_server.remediation: GPO: Enforce password history = 24 passwords remembered

windows_server.title: Lockout threshold 1–5 attempts
windows_server.remediation: GPO: Account Lockout Policy > Account lockout threshold = 5

windows_server.title: Audit logon events = Success and Failure
Unnecessary/risky services not running
windows_server.remediation: Stop and disable the service (Set-Service <name> -StartupType Disabled); Print Spooler must be off on servers that don't print (PrintNightmare)

windows_server.title: RDP requires Network Level Authentication
windows_server.remediation: GPO: Remote Desktop Session Host > Security > Require user authentication using NLA = Enabled

windows_server.title: EDR agent installed and running
windows_server.remediation: Reinstall the EDR sensor from the management console and verify check-in

windows_server.title: Automatic security updates enabled
windows_server.remediation: Enroll in WSUS/Intune update ring; enable automatic security updates

linux_server.title: SSH root login disabled
linux_server.remediation: Set 'PermitRootLogin no' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config; systemctl reload sshd

linux_server.title: auditd and rsyslog running
linux_server.remediation: dnf install audit rsyslog && systemctl enable --now auditd rsyslog

linux_server.title: Host firewall enabled
linux_server.remediation: systemctl enable --now firewalld (default zone drop/public with only required services)

linux_server.title: Automatic security updates enabled
linux_server.remediation: dnf install dnf-automatic; enable dnf-automatic-install.timer (security only)

linux_server.title: /tmp mounted noexec
linux_server.remediation: Add noexec,nosuid,nodev to the /tmp entry in /etc/fstab and remount

agreement_types.SLA: Service-level agreement: measurable service commitments such as uptime and response times, with remedies
agreement_types.MSA: Master service agreement: the umbrella legal terms that govern all future work orders
agreement_types.SOW/WO: Statement of work / work order: the specific deliverables, scope and timeline for one engagement
agreement_types.NDA: Non-disclosure agreement: obligation to keep shared information confidential
agreement_types.MOU: Memorandum of understanding: a statement of shared intent, usually NOT legally binding
agreement_types.MOA: Memorandum of agreement: a more formal, conditional agreement between parties on specific responsibilities
agreement_types.BPA: Business partnership agreement: how partners share profits, losses, decisions and responsibilities

concepts.CRL: A list, published by a CA, of serial numbers it has revoked; clients download it periodically
concepts.OCSP: A protocol that asks the CA's responder for the real-time status of ONE certificate
concepts.OCSP stapling: The web server fetches its own signed OCSP response and attaches it to the TLS handshake
concepts.CSR: A request containing the public key and subject details that is sent to a CA to obtain a certificate
concepts.Wildcard certificate: A certificate whose name like *.example.com covers exactly one level of subdomains
concepts.SAN: The certificate extension that lists every DNS name (and IP) the certificate is valid for
concepts.Root of trust: A self-signed CA certificate that clients trust directly because it is in their trust store
concepts.Key escrow: A trusted third party holds a copy of private keys so data can be recovered
concepts.Certificate pinning: An application only accepts a specific certificate or public key for a site, even if another CA-signed one is presented
concepts.Self-signed certificate: A certificate signed by its own key, not by a CA the client already trusts

environment_types.known: Known environment (formerly white box): testers get full details such as network diagrams, source code and credentials.
environment_types.partially_known: Partially known environment (formerly gray box): testers get some information, e.g. a user account or an IP range, but not full documentation.
environment_types.unknown: Unknown environment (formerly black box): testers get no prior information and must discover everything, like an outside attacker.

audit.passive_recon_note: Passive reconnaissance only reads public third-party sources (search engines, WHOIS, certificate transparency logs) and sends nothing to client systems, so it may run outside the testing window hours. It still needs signed, in-date authorization and an in-scope target: the RoE covers the whole engagement, not only the packets.

osint_search.description: Search engines, social media and public filings about the client (OSINT)

whois_dns_lookup.description: WHOIS records and public DNS data from third-party resolvers

cert_transparency.description: Read certificate transparency logs to find subdomains

port_scan.description: Send probes to target ports to find listening services

banner_grab.description: Connect to services and read their version banners

vuln_scan.description: Run a vulnerability scanner against target hosts

web_app_test.description: Attempt injection and authentication attacks on a web app

password_spray.description: Try a few common passwords against many accounts

physical_tailgating.description: Follow staff through a secured door

dos_flood.description: Flood a service to make it unavailable (denial of service)

prod_data_modify.description: Change records in a production database

pentest_types.offensive: Offensive testing (red team): attack the organisation the way an adversary would to find exploitable weaknesses.
pentest_types.defensive: Defensive testing (blue team): test how well detection and response controls identify and stop attacks.
pentest_types.integrated: Integrated testing (purple team): attackers and defenders work together, sharing results to improve controls in real time.
pentest_types.physical: Physical penetration testing: test locks, badges, guards and doors, e.g. tailgating into a data centre.

INTERNAL_AUDIT.definition: Internal audit: the organisation's own audit function checks compliance with policies and laws and reports to the audit committee.

SELF_ASSESSMENT.definition: Self-assessment: a team reviews its own controls against a standard or checklist; quick and cheap but not independent.

REGULATORY_EXAMINATION.definition: Regulatory examination: a government regulator inspects the organisation to verify it meets legal requirements.

INDEPENDENT_THIRD_PARTY_AUDIT.definition: Independent third-party audit: an outside firm with no stake in the result audits the controls and gives an unbiased opinion.

ATTESTATION.definition: Attestation: an independent auditor formally states (attests) that controls are in place and working, e.g. a SOC 2 Type II report.

regulator_requires.why: a regulator mandates it, so the regulator (or its examiners) performs an external examination

audit_committee.why: the board's audit committee oversees internal audit; when independence is required an outside firm is engaged

compliance_review.why: checking adherence to internal policy and law is the internal audit compliance function

customer_soc2.why: a customer wants a SOC 2 report, which is an independent auditor's attestation

self_check.why: a team checking its own controls is a self-assessment; it cannot satisfy an independence requirement

iac._comment: Lab 20 IaC gate. A check PASSES only when the declared property satisfies 'op'; a missing property FAILS (deny by default).

checks.title: Public storage bucket ACL
checks.rationale: A public bucket exposes every object to the internet (data exposure is the #1 cloud breach cause).
checks.fix: Set acl = "private" and enable block-public-access; serve public content through a CDN.

checks.title: Storage not encrypted at rest
checks.rationale: Data at rest must be encrypted so lost media or a mis-scoped snapshot does not leak it.
checks.fix: Set encryption_at_rest = true with a KMS-managed key.

checks.title: Access logging disabled
checks.rationale: Without access logs there is no audit trail for incident response.
checks.fix: Set logging = true and ship logs to the central SIEM bucket.

checks.title: Admin/database port open to the internet
checks.rationale: SSH/RDP/database ports reachable from 0.0.0.0/0 invite brute force and exploitation.
checks.fix: Restrict the source CIDR to a bastion/VPN range (RFC 1918) or use a managed session service.

checks.title: VM disk not encrypted
checks.rationale: Unencrypted volumes and their snapshots expose data at rest.

checks.title: VM has a public IP
checks.rationale: Directly exposed hosts enlarge the attack surface; put them behind a load balancer or bastion.
checks.fix: Set public_ip = false and reach the VM through the load balancer or a bastion.

checks.title: Database publicly accessible
checks.rationale: A database endpoint on the internet bypasses network segmentation.
checks.fix: Set publicly_accessible = false and place it in a private subnet.

checks.title: Database not encrypted at rest
checks.rationale: Database files, replicas and backups must be encrypted at rest.
checks.fix: Set encryption_at_rest = true (re-create from an encrypted snapshot).

checks.title: Backup retention too short
checks.rationale: Short retention hurts ease of recovery (e.g. ransomware found after a week).

checks.title: IAM policy grants * on *
checks.rationale: Action '*' on resource '*' is full admin: it breaks least privilege and maximises blast radius.
checks.fix: Grant only the specific actions on the specific resource ARNs the role needs.

checks.title: Privileged container
checks.rationale: A privileged container can reach the host kernel and devices: container escape.
checks.fix: Set privileged = false and add only the specific capabilities needed.

checks.title: Container runs as root
checks.rationale: Root inside the container makes escape and tampering easier.
checks.fix: Set run_as_root = false (USER non-root in the image, runAsNonRoot).

checks.title: Secrets in plaintext environment variables
checks.rationale: Plaintext secrets in config leak through logs, consoles and the IaC repo itself.
checks.fix: Reference the secret from a secrets manager/vault instead of the environment.

checks.title: Listener allows plain HTTP
checks.rationale: Data in transit must be encrypted with TLS.
checks.fix: Set https_only = true and redirect port 80 to 443.

checks.title: Critical resource in a single availability zone
checks.rationale: A resource tagged critical needs high availability: one zone is a single point of failure.
checks.fix: Deploy across at least 2 availability zones (multi-AZ replica / auto-scaling group).

checks.title: Missing required tags
checks.rationale: Owner and data_classification tags drive accountability, data handling and cost allocation.

architecture_models.serverless: Code runs as functions on provider-managed compute: you never patch an OS, but you still secure code, permissions and secrets.
architecture_models.microservices: An application split into small independently deployed services talking over APIs: more API surface, smaller blast radius.
architecture_models.containerization: Applications packaged with their dependencies sharing the host kernel: fast and portable, but a kernel escape hits every container.
architecture_models.virtualization: Multiple guest OSes on one hypervisor: VM escape and VM sprawl are the key risks.
architecture_models.air-gapped network: Physical isolation with no network connection to other networks: strongest isolation, but updates and data move by removable media.
architecture_models.logical segmentation: VLANs/subnets and ACLs separate traffic on shared hardware: limits lateral movement without separate equipment.
architecture_models.software-defined networking (SDN): Network control plane separated from the data plane and managed centrally in software: agile, but the controller is a high-value target.
architecture_models.ICS/SCADA: Industrial control of physical processes on legacy protocols: availability first, often unable to patch, so segmentation is the main control.
architecture_models.IoT: Many low-cost connected sensors and devices: weak default credentials and limited patch availability.
architecture_models.RTOS: An operating system that must respond within strict timing deadlines: security controls must not add latency.
architecture_models.embedded system: Firmware-based hardware built for one dedicated function with limited compute and power: hard to update.
architecture_models.hybrid cloud: On-premises infrastructure combined with public cloud: consistent policy and identity across both is the challenge.
architecture_models.infrastructure as code (IaC): Infrastructure defined in version-controlled templates: repeatable, scannable deployments, but one bad template misconfigures every copy.

compliance._note: All deadlines and periods are configurable ILLUSTRATIONS for learning, not legal advice. Real obligations depend on the jurisdiction, the facts and counsel.

control_attestation.label: Annual control attestation to a customer / auditor

rule_labels.UNKNOWN_REGIME: the regime is not in the policy (deny by default)

data_roles.data subject: The identifiable living person the personal data is about; holds rights such as access, rectification and erasure.
data_roles.data controller: Decides WHY and HOW personal data is processed and is accountable for compliance and subject requests.
data_roles.data processor: Processes personal data on behalf of, and only on the instructions of, the controller (e.g. a payroll SaaS).
data_roles.data owner: A senior business role accountable for a data set: classifies it and approves who may access it.
data_roles.data custodian/steward: Handles the data day to day: custodian implements storage, backup and security controls; steward manages quality, labelling and metadata.

consequences.fines: Monetary penalties imposed by a regulator for violating a law or regulation.
consequences.sanctions: Formal penalties from a court, government or regulator, e.g. restrictions or orders for destroying evidence.
consequences.reputational damage: Loss of customer and public trust after a publicised failure.
consequences.loss of license: Revocation of the permission (license, certification, authority) needed to operate or process certain data.
consequences.contractual impacts: Breach of contract with customers or partners: penalties, termination or lost business.

diligence_terms.due diligence: Investigating and verifying BEFORE and while acting: research, assessments, audits to understand risk.
diligence_terms.due care: Acting as a reasonable, prudent organisation would: implementing and maintaining the controls and policies.

finding_actions.UNMANAGED: shadow IT: onboard it into the CMDB (owner + classification) or quarantine/block it with NAC
finding_actions.MISSING: possible loss or theft: locate the asset, check for a lost/stolen report, consider remote wipe
finding_actions.NO_OWNER: assign an accountable owner (asset ownership is part of assignment/accounting)
finding_actions.UNCLASSIFIED: classify the asset so the right controls and disposal level apply

incompatibility_notes.degauss:ssd: degaussing only affects magnetic media; flash memory in an SSD is untouched
incompatibility_notes.degauss:usb: degaussing only affects magnetic media; a USB flash drive is untouched
incompatibility_notes.degauss:mobile: degaussing only affects magnetic media; phone flash storage is untouched
incompatibility_notes.overwrite:ssd: overwriting is unreliable on SSDs: wear levelling and over-provisioned blocks keep old data; use crypto-erase/secure erase or destroy
incompatibility_notes.overwrite:mobile: overwriting is unreliable on flash; use the built-in crypto-erase or destroy
incompatibility_notes.clear:ssd: logical clearing is unreliable on SSDs because of wear levelling; purge (crypto-erase) or destroy instead

glossary.certificate of destruction: Signed evidence from the disposal provider listing the assets, method and date: proves the media was sanitized/destroyed and transfers accountability.
glossary.data retention: Keeping records for a defined period required by law, regulation or policy before they may be disposed of.
glossary.legal hold: A litigation or investigation order that suspends normal deletion and disposal of the relevant data.
glossary.shadow IT: Devices or services used without IT approval, so they are missing from the inventory and unmanaged.
glossary.enumeration: Actively discovering every device and service on the network (e.g. a discovery scan) to compare against the inventory.
glossary.asset ownership: The person or team accountable for an asset, its classification and its lifecycle decisions.
glossary.clear: Logical sanitization (e.g. overwriting) that defeats simple recovery tools; suitable when media stays in the organisation.
glossary.purge: Sanitization that defeats laboratory recovery (crypto-erase, secure erase, degaussing) while the media may still be reusable.
glossary.destroy: Physical destruction (shredding, pulverizing, incinerating) so the media cannot be reused or recovered.

behaviour_responses.RISKY: open an investigation and refer to the insider-threat team (HR + legal + security)
behaviour_responses.UNEXPECTED: verify with the user and their manager and tune UEBA monitoring
behaviour_responses.UNINTENTIONAL: coaching and targeted just-in-time training; no disciplinary action
behaviour_responses.NOT_ANOMALOUS: close as expected behaviour and document the baseline

at_rest.method: tokenize the PAN (or encrypt it at rest); never store it in clear text

in_transit.method: encrypt in transit with TLS 1.2+ (or send a token instead of the PAN)

in_use.method: mask the PAN to the last 4 digits
mask direct identifiers (e.g. SSN to last 4)

at_rest.method: store only a salted, key-stretched hash (bcrypt/PBKDF2/Argon2), never reversible encryption

in_transit.method: send credentials only over an encrypted channel (TLS)

in_use.method: mask secrets in screens and logs
restrict permissions to the legal team

protection_methods.encryption: Encryption: reversibly transforms data with a key so only key holders can read it (at rest: AES; in transit: TLS/IPsec).
protection_methods.hashing: Hashing: one-way fixed-length digest that cannot be reversed; salt + key stretching for stored passwords.
protection_methods.masking: Masking: hides part of a value on display or in copies (e.g. ************1111) while keeping its format.
protection_methods.tokenization: Tokenization: replaces the value with a random surrogate token; the real value is mapped in a secure token vault.
protection_methods.obfuscation: Obfuscation: makes data or code hard to understand without a key (e.g. code obfuscation, steganography).
protection_methods.segmentation: Segmentation: keeps sensitive data in separate networks/systems so a breach of one does not expose all.
protection_methods.permission_restrictions: Permission restrictions: access controls (least privilege, ACLs) limit who can read or change the data.
protection_methods.geographic_restrictions: Geographic restrictions: allow storage or access only from approved locations (geolocation / geofencing).

sources.auth: Authentication / OS security logs (logon success and failure, account changes)
sources.firewall: Firewall logs (allowed and denied connections, ports)
sources.edr: Endpoint logs from the EDR/antivirus agent (detections, quarantine)
sources.dns: DNS query logs (domains resolved by each host)

rules.name: Log parse failure
rules.description: An event is missing id/ts/source, has an unparseable timestamp or comes from an unknown source
rules.response: fix the collector/parser and re-ingest; an unparsed event is invisible to every other rule

rules.name: Brute force
rules.description: At least N failed logins for one user from one IP within W seconds

escalate.response: possible compromise: disable the account, revoke sessions, quarantine the user's host via EDR

rules.response: lock the account temporarily and block the source IP at the firewall

rules.name: Password spraying
rules.description: One source IP fails against at least M distinct users within W seconds
rules.response: block the source IP and force password resets / MFA enrolment for the targeted users

rules.name: Impossible travel
rules.description: Two successive successful logins by one user from places too far apart for the time between them
rules.response: revoke the user's sessions, require MFA re-authentication and verify with the user

rules.name: After-hours privileged action
rules.description: A privileged action outside business hours (UTC)
rules.response: confirm with the account owner and their manager; revert the change if not approved

rules.name: Log source silence
rules.description: An expected log source sent no events for longer than its allowed gap (monitoring blind spot)
rules.response: check the agent/forwarder and its heartbeat (SNMP trap, agent health), restore collection, then validate events arrive

rules.name: Threat-intel match
rules.description: An event involves an IP or domain on the threat-intelligence list
rules.response: block the IP / sinkhole the domain and quarantine the host via EDR for investigation

rules.name: Port scan
rules.description: One source IP touches at least N distinct destination ports within W seconds
rules.response: identify the scanning host; block it at the firewall if it is not an authorised scanner

rules.name: Malware not blocked
rules.description: The EDR/antivirus agent detected malware but did not block or quarantine it
rules.response: quarantine the host via EDR, remove the malware, then validate with a rescan before release

suppressions.reason: travels often, uses a cloud VPN

tools.SIEM: Aggregates and correlates logs from many sources and raises alerts
tools.SCAP: Standard formats (e.g. XCCDF, OVAL) so tools can check configurations against a benchmark automatically
tools.Benchmarks: Published secure-configuration guides such as CIS Benchmarks
tools.Agent-based monitoring: Software installed on the host that collects and forwards data
tools.Agentless monitoring: Collects data remotely (e.g. over SSH, WMI or an API) without installing software
tools.SNMP traps: Unsolicited alert messages a network device sends to the management station
tools.NetFlow: Records metadata about traffic flows (who talked to whom, ports, volume), not the content
tools.DLP: Detects and blocks sensitive data leaving the organisation
tools.Vulnerability scanner: Probes systems for known weaknesses and missing patches

activities.Log aggregation: Collecting logs from many systems into one place in a common format
activities.Alert tuning: Adjusting rules, thresholds and suppressions to cut false positives without missing real attacks
activities.Quarantine: Isolating a suspect host or file so it cannot spread or communicate
activities.Archiving: Keeping logs for the retention period required by policy or law
activities.Validation: Confirming that a remediation actually worked, e.g. by rescanning

finding_definitions.CORRELATED: The account is linked to exactly one known identity (or a service account to an active named owner) and needs no action.
finding_definitions.ORPHAN: An account that no identity in the authoritative HR source owns: nobody is accountable for it.
finding_definitions.TERMINATED_WITH_ACCESS: The owner left the organisation (HR status terminated) but the account is still enabled: de-provisioning failed.
finding_definitions.DORMANT: An enabled account with no login for longer than the policy limit (or no login recorded at all).
finding_definitions.PRIVILEGED_UNOWNED: A privileged or service (non-human) account without an active named owner: deny by default.
finding_definitions.DUPLICATE: A second account for the same identity in the same application, which splits audit trails and doubles access.

concepts.authoritative source: The system of record for who works here (usually HR); it decides whether an identity exists and is active.
concepts.aggregation: Collecting the account lists from every connected application into one place.
concepts.correlation: Linking each application account to the person (identity) who owns it, using matching rules.
concepts.entitlement: One specific permission inside an application, such as a group, role or right.
concepts.role: A named bundle of entitlements matched to a job function, granted together.
concepts.access profile: A bundle of entitlements from ONE application that is requested and reviewed as a unit.
concepts.access certification: A periodic attestation where a manager or owner confirms each person still needs each entitlement.

conditional_access._comment: Lab 25: Conditional Access evaluator + just-in-time privileged role activation. Every applicable policy is evaluated; any BLOCK wins; otherwise ALL grant requirements of ALL applicable policies must be met.

grant_controls.compliant_device: device marked compliant by device management (MDM)
grant_controls.approved_app: an approved client app with app protection

policies.name: CA03 Require MFA for medium/high sign-in risk
CA04 Payroll off-network needs MFA and compliant device
CA05 Mobile mail needs approved app or compliant device
CA07 Guests must accept terms of use
CA08 Old pilot: compliant device for everyone

concepts.just-in-time permissions: privileges granted only when needed, for a limited time, then removed automatically
concepts.standing privilege: an admin role held permanently, active 24x7 whether or not it is being used
concepts.password vaulting: privileged passwords stored in a vault and checked out (and rotated) per use
concepts.ephemeral credentials: short-lived credentials created for one session or task and then discarded
concepts.break-glass account: an emergency admin account excluded from normal access policies, tightly monitored
concepts.report-only mode: a policy is evaluated and logged but not enforced, to test its impact first
concepts.legacy authentication: older protocols (IMAP, POP, basic auth SMTP) that cannot perform MFA
concepts.adaptive identity: access decisions that change with real-time context such as risk, location and device
